The dataset for LM2 currently extends only to reference 1105; Torah 114 (reference 1114) has not yet been entered. The source text (torah_114.txt) is a three-sentence personal testimony by R' Nathan about a silent walk with Rebbe Nachman during which the Rebbe uttered a single Yiddish sentence: 'Es hot a panim az me muz zikh fun a hirur zeyer hitn' — it seems that one must guard oneself very much from an improper thought (הִרְהוּר). Nathan then testifies that he understood from the Rebbe's holy tone and movements that the Rebbe had been shown the enormity of the damage of hirur (פְּגַם הַהִרְהוּר). The text ends: 'And it is impossible to describe this in writing.' The word 'בְּחִינַת' does not appear anywhere in the source text. There are no bechina constructions ('X הוא בחינת Y', 'X נקרא Y') and no conceptual parallelism equating language. The teaching is a personal anecdote, not a structured conceptual teaching. הִרְהוּר and פְּגַם הַהִרְהוּר appear in the context of an eitza-type warning ('one must guard from'), not as ontological equations between concepts. Packages cannot be built from the bechina subgraph because the subgraph is empty.
